primary_sources_checked.title: LeetCode 516 — Longest Palindromic Subsequence
verified_claims: The task asks for the length of the longest palindromic subsequence.
A subsequence may delete characters while preserving the relative order of those retained.
The official examples are bbbab -> 4 and cbbd -> 2.
The official constraints are 1 <= s.length <= 1000 and lowercase English letters only.

primary_sources_checked.title: LongestPalindromicSubsequence deterministic Java validation
verified_claims: The candidate implementation compiles under javac 21.0.11.
It returns the official example results and the documented explicit boundary results.
It matches an independent brute-force subsequence-enumeration oracle for all 9,841 strings over {a,b,c} of lengths 0..8.

findings.finding: The candidate directly answers the LeetCode 516 boundary shared by all three source variants and clearly distinguishes subsequence from substring.

The interval-DP state, base case, equal-endpoint and unequal-endpoint recurrences, dependency order, final state, and O(n^2) time / O(n^2) space bounds are internally consistent with the Java implementation.
The candidate covers implementation boundaries beyond the official contract without confusing them with LeetCode requirements: null and empty input are explicitly repository-local defensive behavior.

The reproducible validation is materially stronger than example-only checking because it compares the DP result with an independently implemented brute-force oracle across all short strings in a fixed alphabet.

The follow-ups are problem-specific and cover recurrence justification, O(n) space compression, sequence reconstruction, substring-vs-subsequence distinction, and the LCS formulation; the project section avoids fabricated production experience.
